newsitem.title: USA: GAO says airport costs range $1.4 bln to $10 bln.
newsitem.headline: GAO says airport costs range $1.4 bln to $10 bln.

text.p: U.S. airports will need between $1.4 billion and $10.1 billion annually in the next five years to repair runways, build new terminals and meet other infrastructure needs, the General Accounting Office said in a report released Monday.

Congress asked GAO last year to do an independent assessment of airport capital costs because of a confusing array of estimates it is getting from the Federal Aviation Administration, U.S. airlines and U.S. airports, GAO said.

GAO came up with four estimates depending on the scope of projects and the kind of airports involved. All four estimates assume projects are eligible for federal Airport Improvement Program grants, GAO said in its 38-page report entitled Airport Development Needs, Estimating Future Costs.
Such grants are awarded by FAA and funded through the Airport and Airway Trust Fund that is financed by taxes on domestic airline tickets and other air travel.
GAO concluded it would cost $1.4 billion over the next five years to maintain current facilities at existing airports, but no funds would be available for expansion.
It would cost $2.775 billion to cover "high priority" projects at existing airports, including expansion, and $6.1 billion to cover all projects whether high priority or not, GAO said.

GAO said the pricetag goes up to $10.1 billion if Congress also wants to fund improvements at most airports currently ineligible for federal grants, at proposed airports and at existing state system airports.
The report says airport representatives had come up with a $10 billion projection by including all projects at the nation's 3,300 primary airports whether they are eligible for federal grants or not.
Airlines, on the other hand, looked only at projects eligible for federal grants at the nation's 421 largest commercial airports and came up with a $4 billion pricetag, GAO said.
And FAA estimated costs at $6.5 billion, using only those projects eligible for federal grants but at all airports in the national system, GAO said in the report, GAO/RCED-97-99.
